question.problem:
According to the Chinese remainder theorem, which of the following systems of congruences has a unique solution modulo $105?$ 

$$
\text{I.}\,\{\begin{aligned}x≡1 & (\text{mod}\,3) \\ x≡4 & (\text{mod}\,5) \\ x≡5 & (\text{mod}\,7)\end{aligned}\,\text{II.}\,\{\begin{aligned}x≡3 & (\text{mod}\,5) \\ x≡6 & (\text{mod}\,21)\end{aligned}\,\text{III.}\,\{\begin{aligned}x≡5 & (\text{mod}\,7) \\ x≡7 & (\text{mod}\,15)\end{aligned}\,
$$
question.worked_solution:
The Chinese remainder theorem states that if the natural numbers ${n}_{1},{n}_{2},…,{n}_{k}$ are pairwise coprime, meaning that $\text{gcd}({n}_{i},{n}_{j})=1$ whenever $i\ne j,$ then for any integers ${a}_{1},{a}_{2},…,{a}_{k}$ the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x≡{a}_{1} & (\text{mod}\,{n}_{1}) \\ x≡{a}_{2} & (\text{mod}\,{n}_{2}) \\ \,⋮ \\ x≡{a}_{k} & (\text{mod}\,{n}_{k})\end{aligned}
$$

has a unique solution modulo ${n}_{1}{n}_{2}⋯{n}_{k}.$

Let's now inspect each of the given systems in turn.

- The theorem applies to system I. The numbers $3,$ $5,$ and $7$ are pairwise coprime natural numbers. Therefore, according to the Chinese remainder theorem, the system has a unique solution modulo $3\cdot 5\cdot 7=105.$

- The theorem applies to system II. The numbers $5$ and $21$ are pairwise coprime natural numbers. Therefore, according to the Chinese remainder theorem, the system has a unique solution modulo $5\cdot 21=105.$

- The theorem applies to system III. The numbers $7$ and $15$ are pairwise coprime natural numbers. Therefore, according to the Chinese remainder theorem, the system has a unique solution modulo $7\cdot 15=105.$

So, the correct answer is "I, II, and III."
